subject: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing
related_links: Linear: ENG-2841 (Perf regression canary in prod)
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

Team —

I want to make sure we’re aligned across Runtime/SRE/Telemetry/Product on the production perf-regression canary before we spin up more implementation work.

Why now: we’ve had a few “looks fine in benchmark-lab / staging” cases that only show up under production fleet heterogeneity + mixed load (scheduler heuristics + kernel autotune drift). We need early warning on p95 latency and tokens/sec regressions per model/slice before broad customer impact.

Proposed goals for v1 (internal-only):
- Continuously exercise representative inference patterns (prefill+decode; streaming + non-streaming).
- Produce stable time-series p95 latency + tokens/sec with noise guardrails (warmup, min sample, outlier handling).
- Alert on regressions vs baseline (initial proposal: rolling median of last 7d, with deploy-window suppression), with enough debug context to triage quickly.
- Integrate with existing observability + paging flow; ship a runbook.

Non-goals for v1: external perf SLA feature; also not a replacement for offline benchmark-lab.

Timeline target: ~8 weeks total, phased rollout (start us-east, 2–3 models, then expand).

Resourcing ask (initial):
- Runtime: 1 lead for instrumentation + version tags (plus kernel/scheduler hooks gated on canary tag)
- Telemetry: 1 for metric schema + aggregation/cardinality budget enforcement
- SRE: 0.5–1 for alert policy + paging hygiene + runbooks
- Product: light touch to align with rollout standards + future Console surfacing

I created the parent initiative ticket here:
- Linear: ENG-2841 “Perf regression canary in prod”

Confluence drafts (still rough):
- Perf regression canary overview (problem statement + ownership + status)
- Perf regression canary design (architecture + baseline approach + tagging dimensions)

Could each of you reply with:
1) what you think is “must-have” for v1 (and what we should explicitly defer),
2) any blockers/risks (cardinality, overhead, pager fatigue),
3) who on your side can take the lead.

If we agree by early next week, I’ll ask for a short architecture review slot and we’ll lock the week-by-week plan.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Exec Sponsor, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

+1 on the need.

SRE must-haves for v1:
- Clear paging policy: what pages vs what creates a ticket.
- Suppression around deploy windows + maintenance windows (regional rollouts, capacity shifts) or we’ll get paged constantly.
- Alert dedup keys that keep one regression from becoming 20 pages (group by model + region + gpu_sku + runtime_build, etc.).
- Runbook with a “do these 5 things first” checklist.

Things to defer (so we don’t boil the ocean):
- Anything that requires per-customer slicing or comparing to customer traffic directly.
- Overly granular labels (kernel_id as a metric label makes me nervous; fine in logs/trace fields).

Risks:
- Pager fatigue if baseline is too sensitive + canary variance is too high early on.
- If canary runs in the same queues as customer traffic, it can turn into a self-inflicted incident when we’re degraded.

Resourcing: Tomáš is heads-down on another incident cleanup; I can take the lead on policy + routing and pull Rafael in for PagerDuty/incident-bot integration once we have payload format locked.

Sean


From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 11:17 AM
Subject: Re: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

Agree with the goals.

Telemetry must-haves:
- Metric definitions need to be explicit and testable (p95 for what window; how do we handle streaming first-token vs end-to-end; what’s the denominator for tokens/sec).
- Label schema and cardinality budget *before* we ship. I’d rather start with fewer slices and add later than roll back.
- Ensure canary traffic is unambiguous (source=perf-canary tag) and can be filtered cleanly.

On labels: for metrics, we can support:
- model
- region
- gpu_sku (only for the SKUs we actually run in those regions)
- runtime_build (or runtime_version)
- scheduler_mode (if it’s a small set)

Kernel selection + fallback reasons should go into logs/traces and be included in the alert payload as context, but not as a metric label.

Risks:
- p95 aggregation mismatch between runtime-side histograms and pipeline rollups (we’ve been bitten here).
- Streaming tokens/sec definition can drift depending on timestamp alignment.

I can have Nadia own metric spec + pipeline changes and I’ll review. If we can get the first draft of metric spec into Confluence by end of week, we can start implementation in parallel.

Logan


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 8, 2026 at 12:04 PM
Subject: Re: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

From Product/Rollouts side:

Must-have for v1:
- Treat it like any other production canary: clear “what does green mean,” “what does red mean,” and rollback/hold guidance.
- Alert payload should include links to (a) dashboards, (b) last runtime deploy in that region, and (c) runbook.

Defer:
- Any Console UI beyond an internal dashboard link hub. We can scope a future “Perf regressions” surface, but I don’t want v1 blocked on UX/API plumbing.

I’m happy to review the Confluence overview/design to make sure the messaging matches the rollout standards we’ve used elsewhere.

Marissa


From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 4:46 PM
Subject: Re: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

Thanks — this is helpful. Proposed v1 guardrails based on your feedback:

1) Canary isolation
- Canary traffic must be “small and safe” and not compete with customer queues during incident conditions.
- Implementation detail TBD, but requirement is clear: strict rate limits + priority class (or dedicated queue if we can do it without a ton of ops overhead).

2) Cardinality + tags
- Metrics labels limited to: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode.
- Kernel_id/fallback_reason goes to log/trace fields + alert context only.

3) Baseline + suppression
- Start with rolling baseline (7d median) but with explicit deploy-window suppression and minimum sample size.
- We’ll document pinned “known-good” as a v2 option for release candidates.

4) Alerting policy
- In phase 1, aim for ticket-first on lower confidence signals, page only on high confidence (bigger regressions + stable signal).
- Dedup by model+region+gpu_sku+runtime_build.

Action items (next week):
- Logan: can you have Nadia drop an initial metric spec outline into Confluence (labels + exact definitions for p95 and tokens/sec for streaming vs non-streaming)?
- Sean: can you sketch the severity thresholds + paging vs ticket split (even placeholders) so we can design payload fields accordingly?
- Marissa: if you can review the overview page and mark any language that reads like an external promise, that’d help.

I’ll update ENG-2841 with this alignment and break out the child tickets accordingly.

— Mateo


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 2:37 PM
Subject: Re: Perf regression canary in prod — align on goals/timeline/resourcing

Works for me.

I’ll draft an initial policy proposal with:
- confidence gating (min samples, warmup exclusion)
- deploy window suppression (time-based + annotation-based)
- suggested starting thresholds (we can tune after backtesting)
- routing flow: page SRE first, then handoff to Runtime when confirmed

If you want something concrete to start, I’d suggest:
- Page only when (a) regression exceeds threshold for >=2 consecutive windows AND (b) sample size >= N AND (c) not within deploy suppression.

I’ll post the draft into Confluence and link it from ENG-2841.

Sean
